Winters and linear extrapolation methods for time series analysis?

Hi Nikola,
Thanks for your interest!
I'm not familiar with the methods you mention below, are they are part of the R base package or a third-party package?
If they are written in pure R code, there's a good chance they will run; if they rely on packages written in C or fortran, those will have to be ported to R or Java.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Update, Package reorganization & refactoring
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I mentioned this awhile back... but will just be getting around to it in the coming weeks, so if you've got any outstanding changes
now would be a good time to commit!

Best,
Alex

On Mon, Dec 19, 2011 at 11:31 PM, Bertram, Alexander <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I'm planning some package reorganization over the next week or so to address some licensing issues, clarify the structure of the code, and integrate the new interpreter/jitting compiler.
> I'm not sure to what extent folks have outstanding commits, or are referencing the API in other projects, so I thought I would give a heads up.
>
> First,
> I've acquired the renjin.org <http://renjin.org> domain, so I will be moving all code into the org.renjin package to better conform with java coding conventions.
>
> Here is the basic outline:
>
> module org.renjin:renjin-data
> License: LGPL
> Classes:  vectors and other data structures, and data reader/writer
> (mostly former r.lang),  e.g.:
>
> org.renjin.data.SEXP
> org.renjin.data.Vector
> org.renjin.data.DoubleVector
> org.renjin.data.Environment
> etc
>
> module org.renjin:renjin-math
> License: GPL
> Includes any math routines that could be
> independently useful to a Java developer
> org.renjin.math.xx
>
> module org.renjin:renjin-interpreter
> License: GPL
> org.renjin.interpreter
> org.renjin.interpreter
> org.renjin.compiler
> org.renjin.primitives
> org.renjin.base
>
> The idea being that between the javax.scripting and org.renjin.data classes, java programmers can depend on renjin without directly referencing GPL'd APIs. (I'm still a bit foggy as to the consequences of this-- I would like to license renjin as liberally as possible but renjin is absolutely derivative of the GPL'd R and I want to honor that)
>
> Best,
>
> Alex

messages.subject: @bedatadriven hello, i'd love to get renjin running with a rest like interface on gae.. any tips?
messages.subject_clean: @bedatadriven hello, i'd love to get renjin running with a rest like interface on gae.. any tips?
messages.body_plain:
@bedatadriven hello, i'd love to get renjin running with a rest like
interface on gae.. any tips?

@Centralcontroll sure! Take a look at the appengine demo and
AppengineContextFactory, should be super easy - msg me if its not!

@bedatadriven tried copying class directories and libs to webapp and
uploading the results.. but i get this myrenjin.appspot.com <http://myrenjin.appspot.com>

Hey Centralcontroll,

Taking this off twiter because the answer is longer than 140
characters...

The browser interface uses gwt, so you'll need to compile before
uploading. If you make a copy of the whole sample, and just update the
appengine-web.xml to your own appid, then you can deploy the whole
thing with

mvn gae:deploy

Which will take care of building the gwt interface.

If you're more interested in a restful api, take a look at
LotREPLsApiImpl. You can use this servlet as a starting point for a
servlet that handles restful requests instead of GWT RPC-- it should
be much simpler because if it's really restful you don't need to
preserve state between requests!

I will try to add a sample for restful gae app when i'm back from Chad
after the 23rd.

Best,

Alex
